H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper is fundamentally organized as a hierarchy: top-level tactic selection, middle-level role assignment, lower-level behavior selection/control, with principal behaviors further divided into sub-behaviors.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Tactic guards combine ball zone and possession, while zone and possession are derived from arithmetic distance/threshold definitions such as Euclidean distance to the ball, l/n, l/m, and BP based on distance <= delta.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions trigger tactic selection, role reassignment variables such as rd, rs, ra, per-player behavior execution such as go-to-ball/block/pass/shoot, and final PWM wheel-speed outputs.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The conclusion mentions robustness under possible robot damage during a game, but the paper does not define explicit fault detection, rollback, or recovery transitions.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: For a tactic state, selection guards are in the tactic-selection subsection and Table I, role assignment is in separate algorithms, behavior actions are in Table II, and executable mapping appears again in the appendix.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Domain terms such as counterattack, pressure, block opponent, wait pass, and blocked goal line carry soccer-policy semantics whose full sub-transition rules are not all formalized.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are described narratively and in later tables after the tactic definitions, forcing attribution from tactic plus role to concrete behavior.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Guards combine zone predicates, possession predicates, Euclidean distances, threshold comparisons, min-distance selection, and boolean exclusions over agents.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Each parent tactic performs internal role-assignment behavior before its role-specific child behavior executions, as shown by the tactic cases and coach-assignment algorithms.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: There is global condition monitoring and tactic reselection, but no explicit from-any-state fault or recovery escape rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: The architecture has a tactic-role-behavior hierarchy with default entry into role assignment and behavior dispatch, but no explicit deep pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: At least four tactic guards partition zone and possession, and their predicates depend on arithmetic distance and threshold definitions where consistency checking is useful.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Periodic monitoring of environmental conditions and the zone/possession change rule apply globally across tactical modes, matching a parent-level during or forced-transition pattern.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: The paper mainly names abstract behavior actions such as go for ball, block opponent, wait pass, and shoot/pass, while the appendix ultimately maps them to concrete wheel-speed outputs.

one_line_pitch: A strong stress test because one compact robot-soccer controller requires nested tactic-role-behavior modeling, arithmetic guarded role allocation, global condition monitoring, and nontrivial behavior actions.
rationale: The paper provides a genuine hierarchical controller rather than a flat event list: tactics, roles, behaviors, and sub-behaviors are all part of the decision architecture. Its guards use both boolean game conditions and arithmetic/geometric predicates, while actions include role-variable updates and robot behavior commands. The main weakness as a stress-test case is the lack of an explicit fault-recovery model, but the hierarchy, guards, actions, and cross-section attribution traps are strong enough for candidate status.
